Which of the following transactions **decreases** the Cash Realizable Value of Accounts Receivable?
Recording an adjusting entry for Bad Debt Expense at year-end
Writing off a specific uncollectible customer account under the Allowance Method
Collecting cash from a customer on account
Reinstating a previously written-off customer account

Recording Bad Debt Expense increases Allowance for Doubtful Accounts (a contra-asset), which directly reduces Net/Cash Realizable Value of AR. (Write-offs and collections reduce AR and Allowance/Cash equally without changing net AR value—actually collections replace AR with Cash, reducing AR itself, whereas Bad Debt Expense reduces Net AR without bringing in Cash!)

Under IFRS (IFRS 9), how must companies estimate credit losses on trade accounts receivable?
Using an **Expected Credit Loss (ECL)** model (such as a provision matrix / aging schedule) that incorporates historical data, current conditions, and forward-looking forecasts
Only after a customer declares bankruptcy (Direct Write-Off)
Always using exactly 2% of total assets

If a company sells goods to a customer on account for $10,000, terms 2/10, n/30, and records receivables using the **Net Method**, at what amount is Accounts Receivable initially debited?

Under the net method, receivables and sales are initially recorded net of the available cash discount ($10,000 × 98% = $9,800), and any forfeited discount is later credited to Sales Discounts Forfeited.

In evaluating a company's receivables quality, which warning sign indicates aggressive or improper revenue recognition?
Accounts Receivable is growing significantly faster than Net Sales, accompanied by a sharp rise in Average Collection Period
Accounts Receivable Turnover is increasing steadily
Bad Debt Expense as a percentage of credit sales remains stable
Cash collections closely track reported Net Sales

When Accounts Receivable balloons much faster than Net Sales and collection days lengthen dramatically, the company may be loosening credit standards excessively or recording premature/fictitious sales.
